events.text: A travelling tea-seller is going on about {oh_house}: {oh_years} years old, they say, with good stairs and bad cooks, and the disciples all fold their sleeves the same odd way. You find you have stopped drinking. You could show him that fold. You have no idea how you could show him that fold.

effects.log: He tells you, and draws it in spilled tea. You go on looking at the table after he has left.

choices.text: Tell him the cooks were always bad

effects.log: He laughs and asks when you were there. You open your mouth, and nothing comes.

events.text: Some young people on the road wear a badge you do not know, and they are going home for the founding day of {oh_house}. They sing the founding song on the way. It has a verse in it about a broken ladle. For no reason at all, you laugh out loud on the public road, and then your eyes sting.

choices.text: Ask them who the song is about

effects.log: They do not really know. "The Founder, I suppose. It was a long time ago." They are very nice about it.
You walk on quickly. The verse about the ladle stays with you for three days.

events.text: In a market you pass an old man selling off robes, cheap, with the badge picked out. {oh_House}, he says, was a great gate once. There are eleven disciples up there now, and a leak. You pick up one of the robes. You do not need a robe. You buy it, and you could not say why.

effects.log: "{oh_head}, poor soul. Means well." He folds the rest with great care.

choices.text: Give him more than he asked

effects.log: He looks at the silver, then at you. "Did you know them?" he asks. You say no.

events.text: Someone at the inn is telling {oh_house} as a joke: the sect with more tablets than students. People laugh. It is a good joke. You are holding your cup hard enough to feel it creak, and the person beside you has moved along the bench.

effects.log: You put the cup down. You pay, and you go out, and you stand in the yard for a time looking east.

choices.text: Ask them to tell a different one

effects.log: You ask very pleasantly. They tell a different one. Nobody is quite sure why the room has gone so quiet.

events.text: The matchmaker has a long list and she is enjoying it. "And of course {oh_house}, if you could ever get a word in there: {oh_years} years, the same tablets, the same terrible crest." She shows you the crest, on a fan. It really is terrible. You feel you ought to apologise to someone.

choices.text: Ask what the crest is meant to be

effects.log: "Nobody knows," she says happily. "A goose? It is a very old goose." You do know. You keep it to yourself.
You change the subject. She goes on down the list. You go on looking at the fan.

events.text: You hear it from a carter: {oh_head} of {oh_house} has built a new wing, and the whole county went to the feast. He describes the old hall with its low door that everyone bangs their head on. You touch your forehead. You cannot think why you did that.

choices.text: Ask if they ever raised that door

effects.log: "Raise it? They would sooner raise the dead. It is tradition by now." You are unreasonably pleased.
You say nothing, and the cart goes on, and you sit with your hand over a place that does not hurt.

events.text: A very old servant is begging at the temple gate with a family register under one arm, because it was the last thing left to save. {oh_House} has come to that, he says. Six fields. You should not be able to read that hand from here. You can.

choices.text: Give him enough for the winter

effects.log: He tries to bless you in the name of the house. You ask him not to, rather sharply, and then you apologise.

choices.text: Ask to see the first page

effects.log: He shows you, with great suspicion. You look for some time, and you hand it back very gently. Nothing there is news to you. That is the trouble.

events.text: It is in the news from the east, between the price of salt and a flood: the cousins of {oh_house} have gone to law against {oh_head} over what is left. You read it twice. You have never had any dealings with those people. You would like very much to knock their heads together.

effects.log: You put it down. You have a good many things to do. You do not do any of them until after supper.

choices.text: Send them something, with no name on it

effects.log: It goes by a bonded carrier, and it comes from nobody. You will never hear what became of it.

events.text: The Great Families have a new way of mentioning {oh_house}: as though it had always been there. {oh_gens} heads of it now. At a dinner someone recites the head of the first generation's saying about silver and water, and gets it wrong. You correct them, before you have thought. There is a small silence.

effects.log: You say you read it somewhere. It is not written down anywhere, as far as you know. They let it pass.
You eat. A nephew of theirs looks at you, puzzled, for most of the rest of the meal.

events.text: A merchant shows you what he says is a letter of credit from {oh_house}, and it is good anywhere east of the river. The seal is worn. You know why it is worn on that side: the first one was cut by somebody who was left-handed and in a hurry. You hand it back very quickly, because your hand is not quite steady.

choices.text: Ask what the house is like now

effects.log: "Rich," he says. "Careful. They have a look about them. Do I know you?" You say no.

choices.text: Buy something, to have the seal on a receipt

effects.log: You keep the receipt. You could not tell anyone why you kept the receipt.

events.text: A family's treasury is not supposed to be gossiped about, and {oh_house}'s is being gossiped about in a noodle shop, in detail. {oh_head} has sold the east fields. You do not know any of these people. You have the distinct feeling that someone has walked across your grave, and left the gate open.

effects.log: You finish your noodles. They do not taste of anything.

choices.text: Tell the gossip to mind their own business

effects.log: You say so in a voice you did not know you had. The noodle shop goes quiet. You leave a tip, by way of apology.

events.text: They are selling a set of ancestral tablets in the market: not selling the wood, they say, nobody would do that, just finding them a good home. The name on the top one is worn away by people touching it. You stand there long enough that the seller starts to come over.

effects.log: It costs very little. You do not know what you are going to do with it. It goes at the bottom of your bag, and you never quite get round to taking it out.
You walk away. Nobody living would blame you. You find you wish somebody would.

events.text: The road bends and there it is above you: the gate of {oh_house}, with its nine hundred steps, of which the two hundred and third is still loose. You have never been in this county before. You are quite sure of that. Your foot, on the first step, already knows about the two hundred and third.

effects.log: You step over it without looking. A disciple sweeping there glances up and says, "Most people trip." You go up, stand in the yard for an hour, and come down again. It is an open gate. You could go back.
You go on down the road. You look back at the bend, and you were always going to.

events.text: You stop to ask the way at a sect gate, and the gatekeeper is very young and very bored. {oh_House}, it says over the arch, in big letters by somebody who could not spell the second word and had it fixed later. You can see the place where it was fixed. You had forgotten that. You had never known that.

effects.log: He shrugs, and takes you. It is a hall. Everyone says so. It is smaller than it ought to be, and you are very polite to him all the way out.

choices.text: Thank him, and take the road

effects.log: He tells you the way. You take the road, and you are a long way down it before you find you have been counting your steps.

events.text: The inn is full, and they send you up to the big house to ask for a barn. The door of the {oh_hall} of {oh_house} is very low. You duck without thinking. The steward has just opened his mouth to warn you, and he closes it again, and gives you rather a long look.

effects.log: He shows you, because it is raining and he is proud. The first one is very plain. You keep your hands behind your back the whole time.
You take the barn. It is a good barn, and you sleep very well, and that bothers you more than anything else.

events.text: There is a festival in the village, and everyone is at the big house of {oh_house} for the bean soup. It is an old custom: the first one made it for the whole county, one bad year. You take your bowl with the rest. Someone has been putting in too much salt for about a hundred years. You nearly say so.

effects.log: You say so. The cook is outraged. An old woman at the end of the table stops eating, and looks at you with great interest for the rest of the afternoon.
You have another bowl. It is the worst soup you have ever had, and you could cry, and you have a third.

events.text: The boundary stone has the crest of {oh_house} on it, and for the next hour so does everything: the mill, the bridge, the school. Then the road brings you past the great hall, with its doors open to the street as they are on the first of the month, so that anyone can come in and bow. So you could. Anyone could.

choices.text: Go in and bow, as anyone would

effects.log: You bow, as anyone would. The first tablet is a long way up. A servant moves you along gently. You had forgotten how long that room takes to cross. You had never been here.

choices.text: Walk on through the crest's lands

effects.log: You walk on. It takes all afternoon. It is good land, and it is very well kept, and nobody on it knows you.

events.text: A column of retainers of {oh_house} clears the road for {oh_head}'s chair, not unkindly, and you are moved into a ditch with a pedlar and his goat. The chair goes by. A hand parts the curtain, and a face looks out at nothing in particular. It has your chin. You did not expect that. It does not, of course. It cannot.

choices.text: Get out of the ditch, and follow for a while

effects.log: You follow as far as the bridge. You are not sure what you were going to do. The goat stays with you for some reason.

choices.text: Help the pedlar with his goat

effects.log: You help with the goat. He tells you all about the head of the house, and you do not hear a word of it.

events.text: {npc}, who keeps the guest roll of {oh_house}, writes your name down without looking up and gives you the third-best room. "The rules are on the door. Meals at the bell. The Founder's hall is open to guests on the first of the month." {He} looks at you at last. "Have you been here before? You came straight to this door."

effects.log: "Mm," says {npc}. {He} writes something else in the margin, and you do not get to see what.

choices.text: Say it is a common sort of layout

effects.log: "It is not," says {npc}, but {he} lets it go, and hands you your key.

events.text: There is a form to fill in, and {npc} of {oh_house} is very sorry about the form. Under "Who sent you" you put nothing. Under "What can you do" you put very little. {He} reads it and sighs. "They will make you a guest, then. No blood, no rank, and External Elder if you live long enough to get it. That is the rule here. It is a very old rule." You know. You wrote it.

effects.log: You sign it. It is a very odd feeling to agree to it, and it is a sound rule, as far as that goes. You remember thinking that at the time.
"The Founder," says {npc}. "A very hard person, by all accounts." You nod. You say you can believe that.

events.text: {npc}, who runs the household of {oh_house}, has seen your sort before. A guest of the house is a useful sort of person with no claim on it, and {he} tells you so, kindly, at the door. You will sit below the salt, and you will not go into the {oh_hall} without leave. You look at the door. You duck.

choices.text: Accept, and ask what work there is

effects.log: {He} has plenty. {He} is rather pleased. By the time you think to look up it is supper, and you are carrying somebody else's account books.

choices.text: Ask to see the {oh_hall} just once

effects.log: "When you have earned it," {he} says. You almost laugh. You are sure {he} heard you almost laugh.

events.text: No one has come to this table from outside in a long time, and {oh_house} does not quite know what to do with you. {npc} puts you with the cousins, then with the tutors, then with the dogs. "It is nothing against you," {he} says. "We have a register, and you are not in it." You know the register. You know the ink.

effects.log: They take to you at once. It is noticed, and nobody knows what it means. The dogs of this house do not take to anyone.

choices.text: Make yourself useful with the roof

effects.log: You fix the leak over the east room, which has been there for a hundred years. Nobody ever knew where it came in. It does not occur to you until later to wonder how you did.

events.text: It takes four days for {oh_house} to find a place to put you, and three clerks. {npc} is the last of them. "A guest retainer, then. You will be fed. You will not be seen. We have {oh_gens} generations of heads on those walls and you will not be on them." {He} hands you a badge. It has the old crest. You turn it over, and it is on the right way up.

effects.log: You pin it on. Everyone who has ever come here has pinned on one of these. You look quite ordinary. You check in the water.

choices.text: Ask if the old saying about silver is still on the wall

effects.log: {He} looks up for the first time. "How did you know about that?" You say everyone knows. They do not.

events.text: {npc} reads the letter you did not bring, in the sense that you have none, and {he} looks disappointed in you on behalf of {oh_house}. "We are not an inn. But the head is taking on people with skills this year, and you may stay as a guest of the house until someone remembers why." {He} has a great many keys. You could name four of them.

effects.log: You thank {him}. You are given a room with a view of a wall. It is a very good wall.

choices.text: Offer to look at the east granary

effects.log: You do not know why you said that. There turns out to be a good deal wrong with the east granary. {npc} starts to look at you differently.

events.text: {npc} of {oh_house} has found out how you came here, and thinks it is the funniest thing {he} ever heard. At supper {he} has you pass the salt, and then pass it back. "Our guest wishes to be useful," {he} says. "Our guest should know what a house is. Some of us have been in this one for eleven generations." You look at {him}, for a while.

effects.log: You pass the salt. You pass it as many times as {he} likes. {He} tires of it first, and that is noticed.

choices.text: Say that eleven is not very many

effects.log: You say it quite mildly. It is the quiet at the head of the table that {he} will remember. {He} leaves you alone for a year, and hates you for the rest of {his} life.

choices.text: Pick up the salt and put it where {he} cannot reach

effects.log: It is childish. It is the best thing that has happened to you in months. The children at the far end are delighted.

events.text: Nobody tells you the table has been changed, so you are left standing with your bowl, at New Year, in front of everybody, while {npc} watches with interest. In all of {oh_house} there is nowhere to sit. You built the benches. You do not know that, or you do. You had thought they would hold more.

effects.log: You eat standing up, with very good manners. By the third course an old aunt has moved along to make room, and never says why.

choices.text: Go and eat in the kitchen

effects.log: They feed you very well in the kitchen. They always did. You are not sure who you mean by that.

events.text: There is a ceremony, and {npc} explains it to you, slowly, as one would to a foreigner. It concerns the founding of {oh_house} and the great virtue of those who were there. It is all wrong. It was raining, the money had run out, and nobody was virtuous. {He} is waiting for you to be impressed.

effects.log: You are extremely impressed. {He} is pleased. You go home and laugh until your ribs hurt, and then you stop.

choices.text: Ask if it was not raining that day

effects.log: {He} stares. "Why would it have been raining?" Somebody further down has looked up. You say you could not say why you thought so.

events.text: Your name has been misspelled on the guest roll for some years, in a way that a child would call a mistake. {npc} did it, and {he} wants you to bring it up. It is not much. It is a great many small things like that, at the table of {oh_house}, for as long as you stay.

effects.log: You never bring it up. In the end {he} corrects it {him}self, in a temper. It is the only apology you will ever get.

choices.text: Spell {his} name that way on the next report

effects.log: You do it once, in beautiful handwriting. Everyone on the council sees it. Nobody says a word, and {he} goes rather pale.

events.text: {npc} of {oh_house} wants to test the guest, in the yard, in front of the juniors. "A friendly bout. Unless you would rather not." It is not a friendly bout. {He} has good form, and it is the form of this house, and you can see in the second step where it went wrong some forty years before {he} was born.

ok.log: You put {him} down, not hard. You mention the second step. {He} goes off to try it, in a fury. It is {his} own form, and now it is better.

fail.log: It goes badly. {He} is very pleased, and tells everyone. You go on thinking about that second step.

effects.log: You hold the coats, in front of everybody. {He} has no answer to that at all, and it does {him} no good that {he} has been made to look foolish.

events.text: The younger ones have a game: who can get the guest to lose their temper. {npc} is winning. There has been a dead rat, a false message, and a very good imitation of how you walk. It is an excellent imitation. You had not known you walked like that. It seems to you the old portraits walk like that.

choices.text: Ask {him} to show you that walk again

effects.log: {He} does. You correct the left foot. {He} is thrown completely, and the game goes out of it after that.

choices.text: Teach the lot of them something useful, without a word

effects.log: You pick up a stick, and they fall silent. By spring they are not playing that game. They have started a different one, where they ask you things.

events.text: {npc} is eighteen and has been told that {he} is the hope of {oh_house}. {He} comes to you at night, because you are nobody and it does not count. "I do not know how to be what they say," {he} says. You are the last person in the world who should answer that. You are the only person who can.

effects.log: "Nobody knew," you say. "The first one least of all." {He} looks up. "How would you know that?" You say you have read a lot of old letters. It seems to help.
You tell {him} to get some sleep. It is what you would have wanted to hear, and in the morning {he} is a little better, and so are you.

events.text: They have sent {npc} to find out what you know, and {he} is very bad at it. {He} has asked you about the old north wing twice now, in an offhand way, and {he} has the look of someone who has been told to report on your answers. There has been no north wing for a century. You remember where the stairs were.

effects.log: You tell {him} about the weather, at length. {He} reports that. You hear the elder laughing from two courtyards away.
You should not have. They dig there, quietly, the next spring. There are stairs. Nobody at the table asks you anything for some time.

events.text: You have brought a sound plan to {npc}, at council, and {he} does not read it. "When you have been here as long as I have." You have been here a good deal longer than that, as it happens, and you have no way at all of saying so. {He} slides it back across the table with one finger.

effects.log: You take it back. They do it your way in the end, four years late, and {he} proposes it {him}self. It is a good plan.
You read it out, all of it, in a level voice. It does not go well. It goes very well with the two youngest on the council, and that is a different thing.

events.text: {npc} refuses your order. It is a perfectly proper order, for an External Elder of {oh_house}, and {he} has refused it in front of the stewards with a little bow. "Only the blood gives that order in this house." It is the rule. It is an excellent rule. There are days when you would like a word with whoever made it.

effects.log: You bow back, and you give the order to someone else. It gets done. {He} has won the point, and has to watch you not mind.

choices.text: Do it yourself, there and then

effects.log: You pick up the other end of the beam yourself. In a few minutes it is all done, and the stewards have seen a thing they will talk about.

events.text: You find the Founder's old study of {oh_house} is shut to you, and you ask {npc} why. "Family only," {he} says. "There is nothing to see. A table. Someone has scratched a tally on the underside, and we do not know what of." You nod, and go away, and you know what of. It was a very long winter.

choices.text: Say nothing, and be cold for the rest of the day

effects.log: You say nothing. You are cold for the rest of the day, in the sun. Somebody brings you a coat, and you cannot think why they did.

choices.text: Ask if the tally stops at forty-one

effects.log: {He} looks at you for quite some time. "I will have to check," {he} says. {He} does. {He} never mentions it again, and {he} stops refusing you things.

events.text: {npc} tells you, with some surprise, that the house has decided you are not leaving. You are to be a Retainer of {oh_house}, with a stipend and a door that locks. "Six years," {he} says. "Most of them do not last. You seem to know how things go here."

effects.log: "At what?" You say you could not tell {him}. {He} takes it for a joke. You let {him}.

choices.text: Ask for the key to the east granary instead of a stipend

effects.log: {He} laughs, and gives you both. {He} thinks you are joking too.

events.text: They read your name out with the others, at the turn of the year, in the {oh_hall} of {oh_house}, Retainer, between someone's nephew and a very good cook. You bow to the tablets as you are told. The first one looks exactly as it always did. You keep your face very still.

choices.text: Bow lower than the form asks

effects.log: You bow lower. {npc} makes a note of that. You could not have said to whom you were doing it.
You look it in the eye. It is only wood. It says your name, in a sense. You do not much care for the likeness.

events.text: They make you External Elder of {oh_house} on a wet morning, with a seat at the bottom of the council and a robe that nearly fits. {npc} takes you aside. "I want this clear. There is no further. Not for you, not for what you have done, not if you saved the house twice. Blood takes the head seat here." {He} looks tired. "That is the rule. I did not make it."

choices.text: Say you understand it very well

effects.log: You do. It was a good rule when you made it, for reasons you are starting to remember. {He} looks relieved. {He} should not be.

choices.text: Ask what a person could do about it

effects.log: {He} stops looking tired. "A person could marry in," {he} says slowly. "A person could be adopted. A person could wait for a very young head. A person could be a great fool." {He} goes in.

events.text: An External Elder is entitled to a tablet of their own in the side hall, when they die, says {npc}, showing you round. There is plenty of room. You look at the side hall of {oh_house}, and at the row of other people who were useful. Then through the door you look at the main hall. You have rarely been so politely shown your place.

choices.text: Thank {him}, and choose a spot by the window

effects.log: You choose a spot by the window. {He} makes a note. It is a nice spot. It gets the morning.

choices.text: Ask who the first of them was

effects.log: "Nobody remembers," {he} says. You do. You gave that person this spot. You had thought it was generous.

events.text: On the first of the month you go in with the guests. {npc} of {oh_house} walks you past the tablets, one by one, and {he} gets to the first, and stops, as they all stop, and gives you a moment. {oh_founder}, it says. Somebody has renewed the gold. You are breathing rather carefully. It is a very peculiar thing, to be grateful to yourself.

choices.text: Trim the lamp under it, since nobody has

effects.log: You trim it. {npc} starts to say that guests do not touch the lamps, then watches how you do it, and does not.
You bow, and you go on. {He} tells you about the second tablet. The second one was a thief. You liked the second one.

events.text: They have put your death on it. You had not thought of that. {oh_House} keeps the day with candles and a very bad poem, and you stand at the back with the others while {npc} reads it. It gets almost everything wrong. Then it gets one thing right, a small thing, and you have to go outside.

choices.text: Stay outside until it is over

effects.log: You stay outside. A child comes out too, bored, and asks if you are sick. You say no. You say it was a good poem.

choices.text: Go back in and stand to the end

effects.log: You go back in and stand to the end. {npc} sees your face, and does not ask. You have a friend in the house after that, of a sort.

events.text: The children of {oh_house} are told the Founder never slept, never lied and never lost a fight. {npc} is telling them now, and you are mending a shelf. One small child wants to know if the Founder was ever afraid. "Of course not," says {npc}. The child looks unconvinced. You drop a nail.

choices.text: Pick up the nail and say nothing

effects.log: You pick it up. You will think about that child's face for some time. You hope they go on being difficult.

choices.text: Tell the child, later, that everyone is

effects.log: You tell them, on the stair. "How do you know?" says the child. You say you are very old. You are not old at all. They take it well.

events.text: It wants re-gilding, and {npc} has been looking for someone with a steady hand and no ambitions. So you find yourself alone in the {oh_hall} of {oh_house} at night, with a small brush, doing the letters of your own name, one by one, in somebody else's spelling.

effects.log: You do it properly. It takes all night. It is the best work you have done in this life, and no one will ever look at it with anything but respect, and you do not know how you feel.
You fix the spelling. In the morning nobody notices at all, except one very old woman, who looks at it for a long time and then at you.

events.text: The eldest of them, {npc}, is nearly blind, and {he} has you read to {him} in the afternoons. {He} likes the old accounts of {oh_house}, and nobody else will sit through them. Today {he} stops you. "Say that again. That name. Say it as you said it." You say it again. {He} does not say anything for some time.

effects.log: You go on reading. {He} sleeps, or does not. When you get up to go {his} hand finds your sleeve, and holds it for a moment, and lets go.
"Nothing is wrong," {he} says. "When I was a child there was an old servant who said it that way, and had it from someone." {He} is smiling. It is rather frightening.

events.text: You look up from the work and {npc} is in the doorway, watching you tie off a cord. {He} has been there for a while. "Who taught you that knot?" You say you do not remember. "No," {he} says. "I do not suppose you do." {He} goes away. There is nobody else in {oh_house} who ties it, and there has not been for a very long time.

choices.text: Tie it some other way from now on

effects.log: You tie it another way. It keeps slipping. You do not know how many years it will take you to learn a worse knot.
You go on tying it. A week later you find a cord on your desk with no note, tied the same way, by an old hand that shakes.

events.text: At the feast {npc} raises a cup to the guest who keeps the east granary, with rather more warmth than the occasion calls for, and {he} goes on looking at you after {he} has drunk. Later, on the steps: "I do not want to know," {he} says. "I have thought about it, and I do not. But stay as long as you like. The house has been easier, these years."

effects.log: You say you will. {He} pats your arm as one pats a horse, and {he} goes in, and neither of you ever speaks of it.

choices.text: Ask what {he} does not want to know

effects.log: {He} laughs, all the way down the stairs. It is a surprisingly young laugh. {He} does not answer.

events.text: {npc} has been sent for from the back of {oh_house}, where the old ones live. They are very old indeed, and they do not come out for anything. {He} has come out for this. {He} walks the length of the courtyard on two sticks, stops in front of you, and sniffs. "Hm," {he} says. "Late." Then {he} goes all the way back.

effects.log: Nobody knows. They are all rather frightened of you for a while. You are not sure that you are not rather frightened yourself.
You bow to {his} back. You could swear that {he} nods, without turning round.

events.text: They let the guests watch the morning form of {oh_house}, from the wall. It is {oh_art}. You have never seen it before. events.text: There is a shrine by the road, put up by people from {oh_house}, with a very small figure in it who has a very large sword. Someone has been leaving it dumplings. {oh_founder}, you read. events.text: An old stranger on the ferry wears the badge of {oh_house} on a worn coat. Halfway across, the stranger stares at you, and goes on staring. events.text: A beggar plucks at your sleeve in the rain, and {oh_house}'s name is on her lips. She is telling everyone, you learn, that the old head of it is coming back. events.text: A street performer is showing off a few forms that came out of {oh_house} some time ago, badly, for coppers. {oh_art}, or the corpse of it. The crowd is pleased. events.text: You are in the middle of a fight that has nothing to do with anyone. It goes badly, and then your body does something you have never done in this life. A turn, a drop of the shoulder. {oh_art}, a witness says afterwards, with awe, and asks you where you studied. You have no idea what to tell them. It has saved your life.

You mean to, for a good many years. You feel better for having meant to.

events.text: You say it at the head of the table: "I was its Founder. In a life before this one." {npc} sets down {his} chopsticks and looks at you with enormous pleasure. "Were you?" {he} says. "How wonderful. Would you like to tell us where you left the treasury?" They are still laughing when you get to your room.

effects.log: You tell them. It is a very funny joke until, some weeks later, someone goes to look. {npc} stops laughing around then. Nobody mentions it to you at all.

events.text: "It is not the first time," says {npc}, without looking up. "One every ten years or so. There was one who claimed to be the Founder's horse." {He} hands you a broom. It is, you gather, the broom they keep for this. {oh_House} has been very patient for a very long time.

choices.text: Go and find out what became of the horse

effects.log: That one is ninety now, and lives by the gate, and looks you over. "They did not believe you either." You have a very pleasant afternoon.

events.text: They make a skit of it at New Year. A child plays you, in a false beard, tripping over a very large sword. {npc} has written it, and it is good. The whole of {oh_house} is crying with laughter. It is the most they have looked like themselves all year, and you find, to your surprise, that you have started laughing too.

You leave in the middle. You can hear them from the road. It is not that they are wrong. It is that you can never tell them what was funny about it.

events.text: {npc} does not laugh. {He} shuts the door. "There have been others. So I will ask you what I asked them. On the night of the fire, what was in the jar?" fail.log: You say the first thing that comes. {He} shakes {his} head, opens the door, and is very courteous. It was close, you feel. It was so close.

effects.log: {He} nods. "No. Of course." {He} opens the door again. {He} seems, you think, a little sorry about that.

events.text: "Then you know {oh_art}," says {npc}. "All of it. Not as we do it. As it was." {He} walks you out to the old yard behind {oh_house}, where nobody goes, and {he} takes off {his} coat, and waits. {He} is very old, and {he} has been waiting for somebody to come and say this for a long time, you realise.

events.text: They give you the first page of the old ledger of {oh_house}, with the hand copied out by someone and three false lines put in. {npc} sits across from you with a brush. "Mark what does not belong." You look at it. It is an account of some money you owe to a woman at a ferry. You have not thought about that ferry in, you suppose, some time.

fail.log: You find two, and you get one wrong. It was good, {he} says. It was better than the last one. {He} takes away the page.

choices.text: Say the real debt was never paid, and ask that it be paid

effects.log: {He} takes the page. Nothing is said. A year later you hear about a very surprised family at a ferry. It changes nothing for you, and you are glad of it.

events.text: {npc} hears you out without any expression. The room is very quiet. "I know," {he} says. "I have known for some time. Do you know what will happen, if I say so out loud?" You do. Half of {oh_house} would kneel, and the other half would cut your throat, and both would be doing it for the Founder. {He} pours you some tea. "So I will not say so."

effects.log: "A very useful guest," {he} says, and the tea is excellent. Nothing changes. No door opens. It is the most anyone has ever given you, and you drink it slowly.
"You duck," {he} says. "Everyone else bangs their head for the first year." You laugh until you have to hold on to the table, and so does {he}, and then neither of you is laughing.

events.text: It is the old one from the back courtyard who answers, of all people. {npc} takes both your hands and holds them, for a good long time, and {he} looks into your face. "You were very hard on us," {he} says. "You should know that. It has taken us this long to get over it." Then {he} asks you if you have eaten.

effects.log: You say so. It has never been said, in all the years of {oh_house}. {He} nods and pats your hand, and it does not solve anything. You eat what you are given.
"I know that," {he} says. "We all know that. It is what we cannot forgive." You eat what you are given.

events.text: {npc} of {oh_house} goes to the first tablet and turns it, very carefully, and there is a small drawer in the back. You had forgotten that. There is a folded paper in it, in your hand. It says: "If I come back, do not give them anything. Make them earn it." {He} reads it out to you, without any expression at all. "So," {he} says.

effects.log: {He} folds it up and puts it back. "You are an awful person," {he} says, with affection. You go on being a guest. You go on being rather good at it.
"Yes," {he} says. {He} folds it up and puts it back. You go on being a guest, all the same. It was a very clear instruction.

events.text: {npc} and the rest of the council have talked about it for three months, and {he} comes to tell you, looking as though it hurts. {oh_House} will write your name in the register, as a child of the house. There is a very long ceremony for it, in which you kneel to the tablets and ask to be allowed to belong to them. You do it all with a straight face.

choices.text: Kneel as long as they ask

effects.log: You kneel as long as they ask. It is the strangest thing you will ever do. You have a claim now, when the seat next falls empty.

choices.text: Ask to write your name yourself

effects.log: You write it. The ink is the same. Nobody sees that but you. You have a claim now, when the seat next falls empty.

events.text: "You understand it does not make you one of us," says {npc}, handing you the papers of {oh_house}. "It makes you someone we have agreed to call one of us. There is a difference, and you will hear about it." You understand very well. You will, for the rest of your life. But when the head dies now, they will have to read your name out with the others.

effects.log: You sign, with thanks. At supper you are moved two places up. Your cousins are appalled. You now have cousins.

choices.text: Sign, and ask what happens to the side hall spot

effects.log: "You keep it," says {npc}. "Just in case." You have started to like {him} a great deal.

events.text: "No," says {npc}. "And I will tell you why, since you have earned that much. It was the rule when the house began, it has been the rule through {oh_gens} heads, and there is an excellent old letter from the Founder on the subject." {He} is quite kind about it. You could recite that letter. It was a very good letter. It was a very bad day.

effects.log: You thank {him}, and you go back to your work. You have been refused by experts, and in your own words.

choices.text: Say the Founder was a fool

effects.log: "Very likely," says {npc}. "It is still the rule." Word gets round the table that you said it, and they are a little colder for a while.

events.text: It goes to a vote at the council of {oh_house}, which is more than you expected, and it goes against you by one. {npc} tells you who, in the corridor, and it is not who you thought. {He} watches you take that in. "There is always next year," {he} says, and then, "No, there is not. They only answer once."

choices.text: Go and have a word with the one who voted against you

effects.log: You have a very civil word. You learn a good deal about the state of the house. You find you can see their point. That is the worst of it.

events.text: {npc} of {oh_house} is brought in to look you over, in the old way, with a chaperone and a lot of tea. {He} has been told what you are: a stranger, useful, of no family. "I do not care for it either," {he} says, very low, over the cups. "But they say you ducked, at the door. I should like to know how." It is the best offer you have had.

"Then I will have to keep asking," {he} says. It turns out that {he} does. It turns out you do not mind.

events.text: Your wedding to {npc} is the talk of {oh_house} for a month, and most of the talk is not kind. You sign the register below a very long list of names. You know the first few. It is an odd thing to marry into your own family, you reflect. There are probably rules. You probably made them. {He} takes your hand, and {his} is cold.

effects.log: You hold on to it. You have a place at the table now that nobody can move you from, and a claim, when the seat next falls empty.

choices.text: Tell {him} it will be all right

effects.log: "Will it?" {he} says, with interest. You find you do not know. You stand there and find out.

events.text: It was {npc}'s own idea, it turns out. {He} asked for you, of all the people in {oh_house}, against the advice of everyone. "They are all so sure about everything," {he} says on the night. "And you always look as though you are trying not to laugh." You look at the ceiling. You put that beam in. You hope it holds.

choices.text: Say it is only your face

effects.log: "It is a good face," {he} says. "Keep it." You have a claim on the seat now, by marriage, and you have a good deal more than that.

events.text: {oh_head} is dead. The heir of {oh_house} is six years old, and looking around at a great many adults, with a certain alarm. The council has been at it for three days, and it has not come to blows only because no one can agree who to hit. Then someone says, in the silence, "What about the guest?" You have no blood in it, and so nobody has to be afraid of you. They think.

effects.log: You refuse. They fight it out. It costs the house a good deal, and it is not your house. You repeat that to yourself several times a day.

events.text: A child is put in the great chair of {oh_house}, with cushions, and the feet do not reach the floor. {oh_head} went suddenly. An old councillor takes you aside and speaks very fast. "There are three people who will kill that child inside the year. You are the only one in this house who wants nothing." You look at the tablets. You think that is the funniest thing you have ever heard.

effects.log: You hold it. You sit a step below the chair, with the papers. In the first week you do something very unpleasant to one of the three, and the other two come to pay their respects.

choices.text: Tell them to find someone else

effects.log: You tell them to find someone else. They do, in a hurry. You see the child at festivals, for a while.

events.text: The child of {oh_house} is grown. The new head comes to you on the morning of the day, in the formal robe, and you have the seal on the table. There are a good many people who would be very glad if you kept it, and you have made sure of that. You have made the house great. They would follow you. It is the first thing you have ever wanted for yourself, in this hall.
