You do not get up. There is a long silence, in which everyone works it out. By evening it is done, and some people have died of it, and you are in the great chair. It fits. You always knew it would.

events.text: You have taught the heir of {oh_house} everything. It was the only way to keep them alive. You have taught them so well that they looked up from the accounts last week and said, very politely, "I think I should take these now." So. Your own work has come for you. You are not surprised, and you are extremely proud, and you could have them killed.

effects.log: You give them the keys. "Was it hard?" they ask. You say it was nothing. You have taught them to know when someone is lying. They are good enough not to say so.

choices.text: Tell them they are not ready, and mean to make it true

effects.log: It takes a month. They are very good. You are better, and you were here first, in more ways than they know. You sit in the great chair afterwards with the door shut, for quite some time.

events.text: {oh_head} is dead, with no one ready. They read the names out in the {oh_hall} of {oh_house}: the cousins, the branch lines, and at the end, quite low, yours. There is a long silence. Then an old woman at the back says, "Well, it would serve us right." It is, you gather, a vote. They are all looking at you.

effects.log: You stand up. It is a short walk, and it takes a long time. You sit down in the seat you had built, with no blood in you, and they bring you the seal, and you hold it a little to the left, where it always wanted to go.

choices.text: Say the blood should have it

effects.log: You say so. You name a cousin, the least bad of them. It is the most extraordinary thing that has ever been done at that table. You go back to your window. You will never quite know why you did it.

events.text: {oh_House} is in trouble. {oh_head} is dead, and the heir is a fool, and the whole council knows it, and so does the whole county. They come to your room at night, three old people with one lamp. "You have the claim," one says. "You married in, or we wrote you in. We do not like it. We have thought about it and we would like to be alive next year."

effects.log: You say yes. They look, all three of them, as if they had been hoping you would refuse. In the morning you have a seal and a very large number of enemies, and the granary accounts have never been better.

choices.text: Say no, and help the fool

effects.log: You say no. You spend the next ten years making the fool look as if he knew what he was doing. It is the hardest thing you have ever done. It works rather well.

events.text: It comes to you as a letter of three lines, in the head's own hand, dated the week before {oh_head} died: "Whoever you are, you have run this house better than I did for some time. I have told them so. Do what you like about it. I would not." You read it in the granary. They are ringing the bell, and you are the only one who has stopped work.

choices.text: Go up and take the seat

effects.log: You go up. They have left the chair empty, and they have left a path to it. Nobody bows until you are sitting down.

choices.text: Burn the letter, and go back to the sums

effects.log: You burn it. You go back to the sums. They ring the bell for someone else in the end, and you send over the figures, and they are very good figures.

events.text: They ring the bell of {oh_house} all night, and in the morning {oh_head} sits in the great chair, as the new head of a house with {oh_gens} heads behind them. Everyone files past. You file past. {oh_head} looks you over, as a new owner looks over the furniture, and asks who you are. They tell {oh_head}. "Oh," says the new head. "That one."

effects.log: You bow, correctly. It is your {oh_gens}th head of this house, one way and another. You are starting to know what to look for.

choices.text: Send up the granary accounts, unasked

effects.log: You send them up. It is a kind of introduction. They come back, the next morning, with a question about the third column. It is the right question.

events.text: There is a new head of {oh_house}, then. {oh_head} was the only one there had been for some time who ever said good morning to you. You find yourself very low about it. Nobody else in the house thinks of you as somebody who might be sad, so you go and fix a gate.

effects.log: You fix it. It did not need fixing, particularly. It swings very well.

choices.text: Light something, in the side hall

effects.log: You are allowed, as External Elder or anything like it. You do it at night, so that nobody will ask.

events.text: The succession at {oh_house} is smooth, by its standards: nobody has been poisoned, and the two who were thinking about it have gone abroad. {oh_head} takes the seat. You watch, from the bottom of the hall, and you think that it was a good decision to make it hard, all those years ago. It was. You would still like to know what it would feel like to be asked.

effects.log: You go back to your work. It is good work. You are, you keep finding, very good at this.

choices.text: Go and offer your service to the new head, in person

effects.log: You go up and offer it. They are surprised. It is noticed. It does you no harm at all.

events.text: You have been a long time on this council. You know which stair creaks, and you know {oh_head}'s habits better than they do, because you made the house that made them. Tonight the door of the {oh_hall} of {oh_house} is open, and they are alone in there, and they look up. They do not look surprised. They reach for the sword on the wall.

ok.log: It is short. They were very good. You stand in the hall with your own tablet looking down at you, and it has nothing to say about it, and you have the seal in your hand. You had thought it would feel like coming home.

fail.log: It is short. They were better than you remembered, or you are worse. They do not kill you. They have you put out of the gate, on your feet, in front of everyone, and they shut it. It is a very good gate. You built it.

choices.text: Bow, and say you came to check the lamps

effects.log: You check the lamps. They watch you do it, with the sword across their knees, and you go out again. Nobody says anything. Nobody ever does. It was a very near thing.

events.text: You have the numbers. The retainers of {oh_house} are in the yard, and the stewards have been seen to, and {oh_head} comes out onto the steps in a night robe and looks at them all, and at you. "A guest," {oh_head} says, with some wonder. "After all this time. A guest." It has come down to the two of you, and the steps.

ok.log: You go up the steps. Afterwards they all kneel, the ones who are left. You have never seen anything you liked less. You sit down, because somebody has to.

fail.log: You go up the steps, and you come down them rather faster. The yard goes quiet. Your people find that they had never met you. You leave by the gate you came in by, carried, and you do not come back in this life.

effects.log: You stop. You send them home. {oh_head} looks at you, and you look back, and nothing is said. You are not sure what you have just done. You sleep very well.

events.text: You call for the old form, in open council: a challenge for the seat of {oh_house}, before the tablets. No one has done it in a hundred years. The rule says blood only, and you have had that struck out, in the course of one very long afternoon, by what you know about everybody at that table. {oh_head} stands up and takes off their outer robe. "Well," they say. "You certainly read the rules."

ok.log: It takes a long time, and it is very beautiful, and at the end you are the head of the house. The whole council is on its feet. Half of them will never forgive you. You read the rules: they are allowed.

fail.log: It takes a long time. At the end you are on the floor before the tablets, looking up at your own name, and {oh_head} is breathing hard. The rule on the loser is quite clear. You should know.

choices.text: Withdraw the challenge, with a bow

effects.log: You withdraw it. They look at you for a long moment, and put their robe back on. The council breathes. There is a price for that, in favours, and you pay it.

events.text: The people of {oh_house} do what you tell them. They do it very exactly, with no expression. Then you sit down to supper and find there is nobody on either side of you, in a hall of two hundred. No one is being rude. You look at the long empty stretch of bench. Somebody has polished it.

effects.log: You eat your supper. It goes on like that for some time. You had said, once, that a house should not be easy to take. It was a very good rule.

choices.text: Go and sit at the lower tables

effects.log: You take your bowl down there. They all stop eating. In a while one of them starts again. It is a start, if it is anything.

events.text: A branch family of {oh_house} has gone to law, in another county, and it says in the plainest words that there is someone in the seat with no right to it. It is quite true. They have sent you a copy, with the seals on, and a very polite note. Nobody who knows the first thing about the Founder would ever have let this happen. You read that part again.

effects.log: It costs what it costs. They stop, for now, and they write down the sum. It will come round again.

choices.text: Go and see them in person

effects.log: You go. It is not a pleasant visit. They are quite right about you, and they are a good deal less right after you have explained what happens next.

events.text: Your dead predecessor at {oh_house} had a child, of course. You had that seen to, as you thought. Fifteen years on there is a very quiet young person doing well in another sect, and you are told they have never once mentioned the matter. You put the report down. It is exactly what you would do.

effects.log: You have them watched. They send your watcher back with a very nice letter. Well, then. It will be a long time. You are in no hurry either.
You write. It takes you four drafts. You say what you did. There is no answer. There will not be. You are glad you wrote, and it has changed nothing.

events.text: An envoy of {oh_house} comes up your road with a very good horse and an offer: a seat as External Elder, a stipend, a house in the east. You have made a name, and the house of {oh_head} collects names. They read the terms out with some condescension. "You will not have heard much about us," the envoy says. "We are very old." You give the envoy some tea.

choices.text: Say you will come and see

effects.log: You go and see. You duck, at the door. The envoy sees that, and looks at you sideways all the way to the guest hall.
You send back the horse's weight in very good tea. They are rather offended, and rather impressed, and you find that you care about that.

choices.text: Ask if the old terms still bar a guest from the head seat

effects.log: "Certainly they do," says the envoy, surprised. "It is the Founder's own rule." You say that was very sound of the Founder, and you see the envoy out.

events.text: {oh_head} of {oh_house} writes you a letter in a very fine hand. They would be honoured to have you at the table. They would be more honoured if a certain piece of land went with you, and a certain marriage. It is a good letter. It has exactly the shape of a letter you wrote in another life, to somebody you were about to swallow.

choices.text: Write back in the same style

effects.log: You write back. It is an excellent letter. The reply, when it comes, starts "Who taught you?", and you do not answer that one.

choices.text: Go in as a guest, and keep the land out of it

effects.log: You go, with no land and no marriage. They are put out. They seat you anyway. You are a name, and they collect those.

events.text: You have done well, it seems, and {oh_house} has noticed, and it wants you to know that it has noticed. {oh_head} sends gifts at the turn of the year. They are exactly right, each one. Somebody up there has been keeping a file. A very old part of you is pleased at how well the house keeps its files, and the rest is not sure how it feels about being on one.

effects.log: You keep them, and you say thank you. You are on a list now. It will be interesting to see who else is.

choices.text: Send back something from the old days

effects.log: You send a very ordinary pair of sandals, of a kind nobody has made in a hundred years. There is no answer. They do not send gifts any more. They send someone to look at you, quietly, from across the street.

events.text: There is a plot against you, as there always is at this height, and now you have the names. You go through the list twice. The third name is an elder of {oh_house}, with its crest on the letter. So it has come to this: your own people, or the next thing to it, are hunting you. They have no idea. They think they are protecting what the Founder built.

choices.text: Warn them off, with a letter they will understand

effects.log: You write a few lines about what they are risking. You mention a thing only a very old member of the house would know. They withdraw, and they go on not knowing why.

choices.text: Treat them as you would anyone

effects.log: You treat them as you would anyone. It does not take long. You read the news of it, some months later: {oh_house} is a good deal smaller than it was. You read it standing up.

choices.text: Let them come, and send them home alive

effects.log: They come, and you beat them, and you send them home with their weapons and a few pointers. They are a good deal better the next time. You feel you have been very foolish, and you are in an excellent mood.

events.text: The assassin they send you is very young and very good, and when you have them on the floor you know that form. {oh_art}. They have been raised on it by {oh_house} from childhood, for this. They look up at you with no expression at all. You taught that expression. You did not do it on purpose. It is a thing that comes down.

choices.text: Let them go, and tell them to find something better

effects.log: You let them go. They do not believe it, and they back out of the door. You hear, some years later, of a very odd teacher in a village in the south.
You finish it. You do it cleanly. You send them home with a note saying who to ask about the second step, which was wrong. You do not sleep.

events.text: A letter comes from {oh_head} of {oh_house}, under the great seal. They have been asked to join a league against you, and they want you to know, from one house to another, that they have refused. There is no reason given. They do not know why they refused, the letter says, in so many words. It seemed wrong. They hope you will not make them regret it.

choices.text: Write and say you will not

effects.log: You write, and you keep your word. It is the most comfort anybody has given you in years. You keep the letter with you for a long time.

choices.text: Send no answer, and use what it told you

effects.log: You use it. Now you know who else was asked. It works very well. You are a little ashamed, and you were always going to do it.

events.text: A company marches past with an old name on its banner, and a crest you know, under the colours of {oh_house}. You knew that name when it was six people and a mule. They have got very good at keeping step. Someone shouts the old war cry, as a greeting to the road. It is a very stupid war cry. You thought of it when you were very tired.

effects.log: You shout it back. The whole line turns to look. A sergeant laughs, a very old one, and raises a hand, and then they are gone.

choices.text: Stand and watch them out of sight

effects.log: You stand there until the dust has settled. They do not know you. It is all right. They are in very good order.

events.text: The guard at {oh_house} still has the name of the company you raised. They do the old drill in the yard, on the anniversary, as a sort of pageant, and they get it all right except for why. It was to stop a very particular person going through a very particular door. Nobody has gone through that door in a long time. They do it perfectly.

effects.log: You stay for the whole thing. It is much better than it had to be. You applaud with the rest.

choices.text: Tell the sergeant the door is on the wrong side

effects.log: You tell them, casually. They look at the plan, for a moment. It is only a pageant, they say. The next year they have moved it. It is the better for it.

events.text: They are clearing out an old office at {oh_house}, and there is a heap of letters going to the fire. You are near enough to read the top one. It is unsigned. It tells the head of that day, with great courtesy, exactly what to do about the Hwang affair. Half the great decisions of that century came out of that heap. The clerk says they never did find out who wrote them.

choices.text: Offer to carry them to the fire

effects.log: You carry them. You keep your eyes in front of you. It was a very good hand. They burn much like anything else.
You keep one back, and read it later. You were very sure of yourself. You were right, too. It is an uncomfortable evening.

events.text: {oh_head} of {oh_house} is in the habit, you are told, of writing a question and leaving it in a certain drawer overnight. Nobody answers it, of course. It is an old custom, from the days when someone did. It helps them think. You stand outside that room at night, with no business there at all, and your hand wants a pen.

effects.log: You go to bed. Your hand goes on wanting a pen. It is not your house now, and you have told yourself that a good many times.

choices.text: Leave one line in the drawer

effects.log: You leave one line, in a hand you take care to change. In the morning there is a great stir, and {oh_head} does exactly what the line said. You had better not do that again.

events.text: You have come down for your own reasons, and it was not for this. From up here the land of {oh_house} is very small and very well kept. You could stand in the yard and every person in it would fall on their face. Instead you sit on the wall in plain clothes, for an afternoon. A child comes over and tells you to get down. You get down.

effects.log: It takes almost nothing. They put it down to the Founder. They are not, for once, altogether wrong.
You go. They will never know. It is what you wanted, and you are not sure when that happened.

events.text: An old, old elder of {oh_house} looks up in the middle of a sentence, and looks straight through a wall at where you are standing. Nobody else in that world could have. The elder puts on a very worn robe and comes out to the back mountain. "It has been some time," the elder says. "We did all right." You had not known that anyone was left who could still look at you.

choices.text: Say that you can see that

effects.log: "Well, then," says the elder. They stand with you for a while, in the wind, and they go in to supper. Nobody ever hears of it.
"Nothing," says the elder, very firmly. "That was rather the point." Then, at the door: "The roof over the east room, if you are passing." You fix it.

events.text: Someone you love has been looking at you oddly. It is {oh_house}: you have mentioned it three times this month, for no reason. "Have you ever been there?" they ask you at supper. "You talk about it as I talk about my mother." You have never been anywhere near it, in this life. You look down at your bowl, and you think about what to say to someone who has a right to know.

effects.log: You tell them. It takes all evening. They hear you out with great care, and then they ask whether you were happy there. Nobody has asked you that, ever. You have to go and think.
You say you read about it. They do not believe you. They pass you the pickles, and they let you have that. It is, you think, the kindest thing that anyone has done for you lately.

events.text: A child of the house has come home from {oh_house}, on some errand, very full of it. They do the voices. They do the old steward. They have brought you a present, since you are always asking: a little carved goose, from the stall by the gate, with the crest on it. It is really a very bad crest. You hold the goose for a good while.

effects.log: It goes on the shelf. You move it, a little, every so often. Nobody has ever asked why.

choices.text: Tell the child what it is meant to be

effects.log: "It is not a goose," you say. You tell them the whole silly story, and they think you made it up. They tell it at the gate, the next time. It has started going round.

events.text: You wake in the middle of the night, with nothing wrong. It takes you a long time to get back to sleep. In the morning it is a little easier to get up, and you are ashamed of that, and you do not know why. It is some weeks before anyone mentions, in passing, that {oh_fell} is gone.

choices.text: Ask what became of the people

effects.log: You ask. Nobody knows. They scattered, as people do. For about a year you look at strangers on the road, at how they fold their sleeves.
It takes a month. There is a very good crop of millet on it. You stand there for a while, and an old farmer asks if you are lost.
You go on with your work. It is good work. You have always been able to do that. You wonder, for the first time, if it was ever such a good thing.

events.text: Something you carried has gone quiet. You stop on the stairs, with one foot in the air, and you stand there. A servant asks if you are ill. It is not a pain. It is more as if someone had been humming in another room for as long as you can remember, and had stopped. You will hear about {oh_fell} before the year is out.

effects.log: You go up. They are the same stairs. You sit on the bed, and you find that you know the date, and you will always know it.

choices.text: Light something, for no one in particular

effects.log: You light something. It costs a copper. Nobody knows who it is for, and you could not exactly say either.

events.text: They are reciting the old houses of the east at some school you are walking past, a long list, for the examinations. A child gets to where {oh_fell} should be, and the teacher says "No, that one is gone now, take it out." The child takes it out. They go on. You stay there by the wall, for a while, listening to the rest of the list.

choices.text: Say it under your breath, in its place

effects.log: You say it, once, in its place. Nobody hears. It was a good name. It was about the right length.
You go on your way. You find you are lighter. You would give a very great deal not to be.

events.text: You have a seat to hold and an heir to hold it after you, and your house should be turning into a dynasty, as houses do. {oh_ask} is ready. But when you reach for it, your soul will not close its hand. A soul that has died as often as yours can carry only so much. Ten names still answer when you reach for them. To keep this one, you must let another go.

effects.log: You turn and look at what you carry. All ten of them look back.
You let it pass. {oh_ask} goes on as a good house, and a house only. Your hand stays open. In a good many years you may ask yourself again.

events.text: There is a seal in your hand: {oh_ask}. It came to you by a road you did not expect, and the house takes you for its own. Your soul does not. A soul that has died as often as yours can carry only so much. Ten names still answer when you reach for them. To keep this one, you must let another go.

effects.log: You turn and look at what you carry. All ten of them look back.
You will hold it for this life, and hold it well. When you die it will go on without you, and it will not know you, and you will not know it.

events.text: You stand in {oh_ask} with its people bowing, and your hand on its seal, and you can feel how little room there is. It is like trying to pick up one more cup. A soul that has died as often as yours can carry only so much. Ten names still answer when you reach for them. To keep this one, you must let another go.

effects.log: You make yourself look at them, one at a time. Somebody is going to have to go. It would not be fair to say you do not know how this feels. You have done it to all of them, in your time.
You let it pass. You will do right by it, in this life. Then it will pass out of your hands, as things do, and you will not so much as know its name.

events.text: You bring {npc} the old accounts of {oh_house}, and you stay after the others have gone. {He} has sat on that council through more heads than {he} will admit to, and {he} does not trust anyone who wants nothing. "So what is it you want?" {he} asks, without looking up.

choices.text: Tell {him} you want the house to outlast this head

ok.log: {He} looks up at that. You talk until the lamp needs oil. Nothing is promised. {He} starts sending you the council papers a day early.

fail.log: "They all want that," {he} says, and goes back to the accounts. You will not get another evening.

choices.text: Say you only came about the accounts

effects.log: You talk about the accounts. {He} is a little disappointed in you, and rather relieved.

events.text: {npc} of {oh_house} walks in the old garden at dawn, because {his} knees will not let {him} sleep. You happen to be there, for the third morning running. "You are very bad at this," {he} says. "Sit down, before you hurt yourself. What do you know about the second branch?"

choices.text: Tell {him} everything you know about it

ok.log: It is more than {he} expected. {He} laughs, and then {he} stops. From then on your name is not said at council without someone being looked at.

fail.log: It is less than {he} hoped. "Find another garden," {he} says, quite kindly. You do.

choices.text: Say you know nothing, and help {him} up

effects.log: You help {him} up. {He} leans on you to the gate and says nothing. It is a very pleasant morning, and you have got nowhere.

events.text: {npc} keeps the keys of {oh_house}, and everyone who wants anything starts with a gift. You start with the leak over the pantry that {he} has been complaining about for eleven years. "What is this?" {he} asks, on the dry floor. You say it is a floor. {He} looks at you for some time.

choices.text: Ask what {he} would change, if anyone ever asked

ok.log: Nobody ever has. It takes three evenings. You now know where every tael in the house goes, and {he} has started leaving a door unlocked.

fail.log: "Ah," {he} says. "There it is." {He} takes back the spare key. It was a good floor, {he} says.

choices.text: Say nothing, and fix the next leak

effects.log: You fix the next leak. {He} is very grateful, and {he} tells you nothing whatever.

events.text: The books of {oh_house} do not add up by a very small sum, every month, for years, and you have found it. So has {npc}, you realise, looking at {his} face across the table. It goes to a widow in the east. {He} has been paying that out of the kitchen money since before you came.

choices.text: Say you will put it under repairs, where nobody looks

ok.log: {He} breathes out. "Repairs," {he} says. You are a person {he} can talk to now, and {he} has a great deal to say about the head.

fail.log: You put it in the wrong column, and it shows at the audit. {He} covers it, and you, and {he} does not speak to you again.

choices.text: Say nothing, and leave the book as it is

effects.log: You turn the page. {He} goes on looking at you for a while, and you both go on with the sums.

events.text: {npc} of {oh_house} has mocked you at that table for years. Now {he} has been passed over for the south fields, and you find {him} at the bottom of a jar. "Come to laugh?" {he} asks. There is nothing like a proud person who has just been told what {he} is worth.

choices.text: Pour {him} a cup, and say who else they passed over

ok.log: By the third cup {he} is telling you who voted how. {He} still calls you the guest. Now {he} says it as you would say a friend's rude nickname. You think.

fail.log: {He} throws the cup. "I would sooner eat it," {he} says, and {he} tells the table about it in the morning.

effects.log: You leave {him} to it. {He} is rude to you again by the end of the week, and it is almost a relief.

events.text: You beat {npc} in the yard for the fourth time, in front of the juniors, and this time you stay behind and show {him} why. {He} is shaking with fury. {He} is also, you notice, doing it right. "Why would you show me?" {he} asks. "What are you after?"

choices.text: Tell {him} that {he} is the only one here who can fight

ok.log: It is true, and it is flattery, and {he} knows both. {He} comes back the next morning. {He} keeps coming back, and {he} brings friends.

fail.log: "I do not need your pity," {he} says. {He} goes off to do it wrong on purpose, for the rest of {his} life.

effects.log: {He} does not believe you. It happens to be true today. {He} goes on hating you, a little more carefully.

events.text: A note comes up with your breakfast, in the hand of the head's own clerk: your evening with {npc}, the date, and what you said. All of it, nearly word for word. {He} passes you in the corridor of {oh_house} later, and {he} bows. It is a perfect bow. You wonder how long {he} has been paid to give it.

choices.text: Say nothing, and change what you say at table

effects.log: You say nothing. The whole table of {oh_house} knows more than it did, and it is looking at you now. {npc} is not on your side, and now you both know.

choices.text: Stop {him} in the corridor, and ask how much

effects.log: "More than you would think," {he} says, and {he} is quite calm. "You should have seen it. You are supposed to be so clever." {He} goes on down the corridor. It is out now, all of it.

events.text: They move against your friends first. Then the head of {oh_house} quotes something at you over the soup, smiling, that you only ever said to {npc}. {He} is three places down, eating with a good appetite. You find that you are not very surprised. You taught people like this, once.

effects.log: You finish your soup. {npc} does not look up. Somebody is going to pay for all this, and for now it is you.

choices.text: Quote something back at {him}, across the table

effects.log: You quote one thing, only one, that {he} once said to you about the head. {He} stops eating. It is not much. Your own position is still a good deal worse than it was this morning.

events.text: {npc} stops you on the back stair of {oh_house} and does not look at you. "Do not sleep in your room on the fifteenth," {he} says. "Do not eat what they send up." {He} goes on down. You are very nearly sure {he} meant that as a kindness.

choices.text: Do as {he} says, and be seen elsewhere

effects.log: You spend the fifteenth in plain sight, at the granary, with the stewards. It comes to nothing. The people who planned it have a good look at you the next morning, and they go quiet for a while.

choices.text: Go to the head with it, and let them see you know

effects.log: You mention it, pleasantly, in council. There is a very long silence. It stops, for the moment. {npc} does not speak to you for a month, which is wise.

events.text: "They have started a file," says {npc}, over the accounts of {oh_house}. "On you. Who you see, what you carry. I have put some dull things into it, so it is a very dull file. Be dull for a year or two." {He} turns a page. It is the most anyone has ever done for you at this table.

choices.text: Be dull for a year or two

effects.log: You are extremely dull. You discuss drainage. By spring the eyes have moved on, more or less, to somebody else.

choices.text: Ask {him} to put something else in it

effects.log: You give {him} a few lines to add, and they are very well written. {He} looks at you with new alarm, and you are sure {he} does it.

events.text: {npc} comes to your room in the good robe, on behalf of {oh_house}, and {he} shuts the door. "You are a very useful person. We would like you to go on being useful, in a way that lets us sleep." There is a paper. It is an oath to the tablets, in the old form, that you will never seek the seat. You know that form.

effects.log: You swear it, before your own tablet, with a straight face. They are all much happier. It is a very binding oath, as you recall, and it binds the person who took it. You wonder who that is.
You refuse, politely. {He} folds the paper up again without surprise. "I did tell them," {he} says. They count you very carefully after that.

events.text: There is a better title for you, it seems, at {oh_house}: Warden of the Eastern Estates, with a very good stipend, a house of your own and eleven days on the road from anyone who matters. {npc} is delighted to tell you about it. {He} watches your face the whole time. It is a very handsome way of being put on a shelf.

choices.text: Take it, and go east for a while

effects.log: You go east. They stop counting you. The eastern estates have never been so well run, and you spend a year finding out who else they have sent there.

choices.text: Say the granary still needs you

effects.log: "The granary," says {npc}. "Of course." {He} writes that down. The offer does not come again, and something else will.

events.text: They have found you a match, says {npc}, within {oh_house}: a quiet cousin, of good family. You have been told that it is an honour. You have also been told about the quiet cousin's mother, who reads every letter in that wing. It would make you family, near enough. It would make you theirs.

choices.text: Let them think you are considering it

effects.log: You consider it, for a very long time, with great courtesy. The cousin turns out to be just as reluctant. You have an ally of sorts, and they have their answer postponed.
You say no, and you thank them. The mother sends you a very small gift, with an even smaller note. They are not happy with you at all.

events.text: A strongbox has gone from the treasury of {oh_house}, and it has been found under your bed by a very surprised servant. {npc} has the guard with {him}, and {he} is enjoying this very much. The whole house knows what you are, {he} says. You look at the strongbox. Somebody has done it badly. It is the wrong lock.

choices.text: Show them all about the lock

ok.log: You show them, in front of the guard. That lock was changed before the box went missing, and only one person ever had the key. {npc} goes white, and it is {his} turn to be careful for a while.

fail.log: Nobody is listening to you about locks. You are walked to the gate with your bag, in front of the juniors.

effects.log: You pick up your bag and go, with your head up. It is your own gate. They do not know that. You do not look back until the bend.

events.text: The tea tastes very faintly of almonds. You have been wondering when it would come to this at {oh_house}. {npc} has poured it with {his} own hand, and {he} is watching you over the rim of {his} cup, with great attention, and {he} has not drunk.

choices.text: Change the cups, with a joke

ok.log: You do it well. {He} looks at the cup in {his} hand for a long moment and sets it down. {He} is off {his} food for a good while. Nobody tries that one again.

fail.log: You do it badly. You spend nine days in bed, and you get up thinner, and you know now exactly how this house does it.

choices.text: Set it down untouched and say the leaves are stale

effects.log: You set it down. "Are they?" {he} says. You both look at it. Nobody will be drinking anything in this house for a while.

events.text: They send you out to the north estates of {oh_house} in winter with four retainers. On the second night three of them are not there. {npc} is the fourth, and {he} has stopped pretending, and {he} is standing between you and the horses, in the snow, with a very good sword.

ok.log: It does not take long. You bring {him} home across a saddle and hand {him} to the head in front of everyone, with regrets about the weather. They go very polite for some time.

fail.log: You get away, in the end, by going through the river. You lose two toes, and you come back a month later and take your seat at supper. Nobody says a thing.

effects.log: You have more than {he} was promised, as it happens. It gets you to the next town. It does not stop anyone at home from trying again.

events.text: {npc} rises at the full council of {oh_house} with a list. Your meetings, your letters, your friends, your walks. Read out one by one, it sounds like a very great plot. Some of it is. They move to strike you from the roll, today, and the head looks at you down the table and asks if you have anything to say.

ok.log: It takes the whole afternoon. You answer every line, and you add two that they missed, for the look of it. The vote goes your way by one. You are not liked any better for it.

fail.log: It goes against you by three. They give you an hour. You use it to walk once around the old hall, as a guest may.

choices.text: Say nothing, and put your badge on the table

effects.log: You put your badge on the table, and you walk out. It was a good badge. It takes them a surprisingly long time to get back to the agenda.

events.text: The steward of {oh_house} left a door unlocked. An elder has the guard at the far gate, on a matter of procedure. And the ones you won have been told what night it is, and they are in the yard with their sleeves tied back. {oh_head} comes out on the steps alone, and looks at who is standing with you, and is very quiet for a moment.

ok.log: It is done quickly and nearly cleanly. The people you won are behind you when you sit down. The ones you did not win are already writing letters, and you know their names.

fail.log: You had it all right except the head. You come to outside the gate. Your friends, you learn, have been very surprised to hear about all this.

choices.text: Stand them down, at the last moment

effects.log: You raise a hand, and nothing happens, and everyone goes back to bed. It frightens the head a great deal more than a fight would have.

events.text: Three of them meet you in the old study of {oh_house} the night before, and go through it once more. They have thought of everything. They have even thought of what to do with you afterwards, you suspect, and that is as it should be. In the morning {oh_head} calls the council, and you stand up in your place.

choices.text: Say it, in front of them all

ok.log: They rise when you do. It is the most frightening thing you have seen in that room. By noon you are in the seat, and you are looking very carefully at the people who put you there.

fail.log: You say it, and you fight, and you lose. They look at the floor as you are carried past them. You have made it very easy for them, and they will be fine.

choices.text: Sit down again, with a remark on the drains

effects.log: You make a remark on the drains. The three of them look at you with a very great hatred, and the meeting goes on.

events.text: It is very quiet in the yard of {oh_house}. It is too quiet: the far gate is shut, and the guard is not where you were told. {oh_head} is sitting on the steps with a sword across their knees, and they have clearly been there for some time. "They told me the hour," {oh_head} says. "I thought I would save you the walk."

ok.log: Nobody was meant to walk away from that. You do, and you sit down in the seat with your hands shaking, and you send for the one who sold you. There is no hurry now.

fail.log: It was always going to go like this. You are put out of the gate, on your feet, and the person who sold you holds it open.

choices.text: Lay down your sword, and walk out

effects.log: You lay it down, and you go. {oh_head} lets you. You are not to come back in this life, and nobody will ever say what nearly happened.

events.text: You have the plans for the gate and the first three names for the roll. You reach for {oh_ask}, the way you have reached for the others, and your soul will not close its hand. A soul that has died as often as yours can carry only so much. Ten names still answer when you reach for them. To keep this one, you must let another go.

effects.log: You turn and look at what you carry. All ten of them look back.
You roll up the plans. Somewhere there is a hill that will stay a hill. Your hand stays open, and it is not as light as you would like.

events.text: A good site, a dry spring, and someone willing to carve the board. It is exactly what you have done before. You stop with your hand on the first stone of {oh_ask}. A soul that has died as often as yours can carry only so much. Ten names still answer when you reach for them. To keep this one, you must let another go.

effects.log: You make yourself look at them, one at a time. One of them is going to have to go, if this stone is to be laid.

choices.text: Leave the stone where it is

effects.log: You leave it. It is a good stone. Someone else may have a use for it, and it will never mean a thing to you.
